text:
Alex M.: noticing a surge of 502s from the GPU edge in us-west-2 since the overnight spot reclaim. Root pods are healthy but callers keep hitting old pod IPs after egress IP changes.
Megan L.: do we have evidence endpoints are updated in k8s? `kubectl get endpoints` / endpointSlice show new addresses?
Alex M.: endpointslices look fine and kube-apiserver shows new endpoints within 2s of pod readiness. clients (internal inference proxies) still try old IPs for ~30s then finally fail.
Rui Chen: sounds like masquerade/bypass + conntrack reuse. If kube-proxy is set to --masquerade-all=false and external egress IP changes, conntrack entries can still NAT to old external pair.
Sam G.: can you paste kube-proxy mode and flags? also which CNI?
Alex M.: running kube-proxy in iptables mode, CNI is calico, kube-proxy args from node: `--cluster-cidr=10.32.0.0/12 --masquerade-all=false --conntrack-max-per-core=32768`.
Danielle O.: we saw similar when cloud NAT reassigns egress after preemptions. Clients behind NAT cache 5-tuple -> conntrack keeps routing to the old pod container IP until timeout. conntrack shows entries like: ```tcp      6 179 ESTABLISHED src=10.0.5.12 dst=10.32.3.7 sport=53124 dport=9090 src=34.120.23.8 dst=93.184.216.34 sport=443 dport=51234 [ASSURED] mark=0 use=1```
Megan L.: can you check `conntrack -L | grep <old-pod-ip>` on the node that had the preempted pod? Also check `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` value.
Alex M.: on the node conntrack entries persist for ~120s; tcp timeout est is default 432000 but we have established timeouts shorter at 180s in some nodes (weird).
Rui Chen: Another angle: headless service + DNS TTL. If clients resolve headless svc DNS and cache results (CoreDNS TTL), then when endpoints move across nodes and SNAT changes, client still uses cached IPs. What is CoreDNS configured TTL?
Alex M.: coredns configmap has `proxy . /etc/resolv.conf` default, not overriding TTL. I saw a 60s negative/positive TTL in logs.
Sam G.: so two layers: DNS caching on clients + conntrack entries cause prolonged use of stale 5-tuple mapping. For short-lived pods (GPU preempt), this manifests as transient errors.
Megan L.: quick mitigation options: 1) enable masquerade-all on kube-proxy so 5-tuple includes node source and reduces cross-node stale mapping surface; 2) lower conntrack established timeout on nodes (careful); 3) reduce CoreDNS TTL for headless entries via `endpointSlice` controller annotations or client side caching TTL.
Alex M.: trying 1) enable --masquerade-all=true on a canary node pool to validate. Also need to check calico SNAT rules and cloud NAT behaviour.
Danielle O.: also consider making inference clients open DNS per-request (no long caching) or set dns caching lib settings to TTL 5s for headless svc in the SDK.
Rui Chen: long term: we should document preemption playbook: adjust kube-proxy flags, conntrack tuning, and recommend client DNS TTLs for headless SRV endpoints. Also track endpointSlice propagation lag metric so we correlate.
Alex M.: filed infra-ticket CIN-4821 to test masquerade flip + telemetry. rolling canary now. will report results in channel. :eyes:
infra-bot: Created ticket CIN-4821 (kube-proxy masquerade canary + conntrack telemetry) assigned to @alex.m and @rui.
Sam G.: thanks — if the canary is good we should prepare a staged rollout with monitoring: conntrack entry age, packet drops, 5xx rate.
Megan L.: adding a runbook snippet: ```- If spot preempt: drain node with --delete-local-data - Evict GPU workloads - Verify endpointSlices are updated within 5s - If >30s errors, toggle masquerade on canary - Revert if increased latency observed```
Alex M.: update: canary toggled, initial traffic shows drop in 502 spikes from 1.8% -> 0.2% in first 5m. will keep monitoring until 2213344610.
